page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, it features 16 physical cores supporting 2 threads per core for a total of 32 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation ratio. The processor incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware acceleration features such as Intel AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Network baseline throughput is configured at 6 Gbps, and the server includes no local storage or onboard GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations show strong performance in single-threaded data compression and processing tasks. The instance achieved 33.6 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 13.85 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing in the top 25% tier. Static web serving throughput reached 51.12 GB/sec, while Geekbench single-core, text processing, and image processing scores also demonstrated strong relative performance. In multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks, the server maintained average tier performance, recorded at 35,034.78 in stress-ng multi-core and 162.39 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Small 135M parameter LLM text generation reached 286.26 tokens per second.

The c7i-flex family offers enhanced cost efficiency compared to fixed standard compute instances by providing flexible compute capacity for workloads that do not fully saturate CPU resources continuously. Because local ephemeral NVMe storage is absent, storage must be provisioned externally over the network. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio limits suitability for memory-intensive in-memory databases, but the platform excels at single-threaded text processing, web serving, software compilation, and light inferencing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory, and a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, the server incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Performance testing highlights strong single-core efficiency, with top-tier results in gzip compression (33.6 GB/sec), static web serving throughput (51.12 GB/sec), and text processing benchmarks. Multi-threaded CPU execution and uncached DDR5 memory bandwidth perform in the average tier. The instance provides cost efficiency through flexible resource scaling, making it well suited for web serving, data compression pipelines, software build compiling, and small-model machine learning inference.
